title: Excise tax on your coffee? House leader shuts down suggestion
summary: Previously, a group of liquor makers jokingly quipped that lawmakers consider taxing coffee, citing younger consumers’ apparent preference for it over alcohol

blocks.text: Previously, a group of liquor makers jokingly quipped that lawmakers consider taxing coffee, citing younger consumers’ apparent preference for it over alcohol

MANILA, Philippines – House ways and means chairman Miro Quimbo quickly shut down the idea of imposing an excise tax on coffee, after a group of liquor makers jokingly made the suggestion on Wednesday, November 25.

“The committee will not allow coffee to be taxed,” Quimbo, whose committee handles tax-related bills, said on DZBB Super Radyo on Thursday, November 26. “That (tax on) coffee, that will no longer be discussed.”

During the committee hearing on Wednesday, November 25, Distilled Spirits Association of the Philippines representative Olivia Limpe-Aw quipped that lawmakers might want to consider taxing coffee instead of alcohol.
She cited changing consumer behavior, as younger consumers — particularly Gen Zs — seem to prefer coffee over alcoholic drinks.
“We told Congressman Miro, maybe you would want to tax coffee because the (demand there) is huge, not alcohol. And coffee is expensive,” Limpe-Aw said.
Quimbo diverted the topic in his reply, saying: “Let’s talk about alcohol first. More people might get sleepy if we talk about coffee.”
On Thursday, Quimbo insisted there is no need to impose excise tax on coffee because it is not proven to be harmful.

“Besides, that is very difficult to administer. What kind of coffee? How heavy? With alcohol, you tax it when the alcohol content is higher. How about with coffee? Because it has more caffeine?” Quimbo said. – Rappler.com
